vocabularies.name: mondo
vocabularies.title: MONDO Disease Ontology
vocabularies.notes: The graph's version IRI is http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/mondo/releases/2026-09-01/mondo.owl, the release the normalization fit's manifest names.

vocabularies.name: onvoc
vocabularies.title: ONVOC
vocabularies.notes: owl:versionInfo 1.0.0. ONVOC is published on BioPortal, which serves downloads only with an API key; the URL is a commit-pinned copy in OpenNeuroOrg/onvoc-widget, byte-identical to the file pondie maps against.

vocabularies.name: canonical_task
vocabularies.title: Canonical tasks

upstream.name: HED-task (the HED Task Catalog)
upstream.covers: The 107 hedtsk_* tasks: their ids (`hedtsk_id`), names, aliases, definitions and primary family, and their hedvar_* variations. ns-pond keeps a byte-identical copy at ingestion_workflow/normalization/data/hed-task/task_details.json.

upstream.name: Cognitive Atlas, through HED-task's crosswalk
upstream.covers: Cognitive Atlas task names matched to a HED task, used only as synonyms when matching names; no Cognitive Atlas id is written.

upstream.name: BrainMap paradigm classes
upstream.covers: The 14 tct_bm_* tasks (inventory `source: brainmap-derived`), made from BrainMap paradigm classes that no HED task matched, through ns-pond's ingestion_workflow/normalization/data/brainmap_crosswalk.json.

vocabularies.id_form: hedtsk_<name> (a HED-task task), tct_bm_<name> (from a BrainMap paradigm class) or tct_<name> (a task ns-pond adds from the corpus)

upstream.name: HED-task (the HED Task Catalog)
upstream.covers: 19 of the 23 families, by their `family_id`. ns-pond adds animal_behavior, dyadic_interaction_observation, information_evaluation_and_belief and ingestive_behavior.

vocabularies.name: condition_atom
vocabularies.title: Condition atoms

sources.role: the rules: `ATOMS`, and the family- and task-dependent rewrites in `normalize_condition_ctx`

hierarchy.description: The axis, the id's text before the first ':'.

vocabularies.notes: The legacy entries carry the axis in the vocabulary string and only the value in `value` (`astra condition atom: congruency` / `incongruent`); `astra condition atom` without an axis appears only on unmapped entries. Under this name the id is `<axis>:<value>`, the form the rules themselves produce. The set is open-ended: the rewrites add atoms that `ATOMS` does not list (congruency:neutral, and level:* moved onto another axis), so no value list is pinned.

vocabularies.name: contrast_key
vocabularies.title: Contrast keys

sources.role: the rule: `key = family | target tokens | baseline`

vocabularies.id_form: <task family>|<target tokens joined by ;>|<baseline kinds joined by +, or vs:<baseline tokens>, or ->

hierarchy.description: The task family, the id's text before the first '|'; `task:<study>/<task>` when the task has no family.

vocabularies.notes: A key is computed from the contrast, not looked up, so there is no list of keys to pin; the rule is the release.

vocabularies.name: contrast_set
vocabularies.title: Contrast sets

sources.role: the ids: each row's `set` (5,445 sets), with its `family` and `label`
the code that fits the sets and assigns contrasts to them

hierarchy.description: The task family, the id's text before '#'.

vocabularies.notes: Set ids are minted by a normalization fit and mean nothing outside it, so the release is the fit. The fit directory is not published; only its sha256 is pinned here.

vocabularies.name: contrast_set_orientation
vocabularies.title: Contrast set orientation
vocabularies.notes: Whether the contrast states its set in the set's majority direction. It reads against the same fit as `contrast_set`.

vocabularies.name: medical_role
vocabularies.title: Medical condition role
vocabularies.notes: none: the item says no diagnosis (healthy); comorbid: it carries a prevalence or history qualifier; primary: otherwise.
